target.title: improve(control-ui): compress and cache bundled assets
target.body:
Related: #105889

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators loading the bundled Control UI would transfer uncompressed HTML, JavaScript, and CSS and revalidate fingerprinted bundles on repeat loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now negotiates Brotli or gzip for compressible Control UI responses and applies year-long immutable caching only to package-proven bundled Vite assets. HTML, public root files, and configured roots retain `no-cache`, avoiding unsafe filename heuristics or changed custom-root behavior.

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex; I understand the resulting Gateway behavior and cache boundary.

## User Impact

The bundled Control UI transfers substantially fewer bytes on cold loads and reuses fingerprinted assets without revalidation on repeat loads. Existing configured UI roots keep their current revalidation behavior.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts`: 352 tests passed across four Gateway projects.
- `corepack pnpm check:changed`: formatting, core/core-test types, lint, import cycles, and changed-surface safety checks passed.
- `corepack pnpm build`: production runtime and Control UI build passed.
- Real Gateway HTTP contract (`run_be6a4309705a`): identity/Brotli/gzip bytes decompressed exactly; `index.html` 14,276 → 3,884 bytes with Brotli; entry bundle 782,854 → 205,088 bytes; bundled assets immutable, HTML no-cache.
- Latest-base Crabbox proof (`run_4172bb521721`): focused tests and `check:changed` passed on the rebased commit.
- Fresh autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; overall patch correct (0.91 confidence).
